answer: Grind a lump of copper ore into fine pigment at first light, then paint a fresh yarrow sprig onto a flat river stone, photographed with a timestamp and a witness beside the stone log. Two pigment keepers verify the photograph against the copper registry and the stone log within five days. A copied photograph, the wrong stone, or a missing log entry voids the season, burns the 60-credit stake, and bars the sponsor for a year. One honest painter spends 60 credits; faking 1,000 entries needs 1,000 copper grindings and 1,000 yarrow paintings.
